title: Stability of Causal Representation Recovery from Paired Interventions near Critical Points
banked_reason: terminal:laundering — the final scoped attempt asserted the load-bearing strip-to-corner inequality rather than proving it, leaving the promised sharp full-class modulus unproved.
gap_reasons: The proposal promised the matching full-class exponent, but the theorem proved only a nonmatching lower/upper bracket.
Equation (8) is essentially the desired strip-to-corner inequality and is asserted after an informal ‘finite recurrence’.
The required effective certified sieve, orbit objective, and explicit calibration were also not supplied.
proof_attempt_summary: The run established an exact synthetic-product identity, exact zero-law identification, a sharp radial-subclass 3/4 modulus, and a conservative full-class bracket. Its final attempt at the promised sharp arbitrary-map result collapsed because the strip-to-corner coercivity estimate was restated rather than proved, with nonlinear normalization and critical-scale absorption still unjustified; the effective certified statistical sieve and orbit calibration also remain open.
tldr: Complete paired interventions yield a synthetic product law and ratio residuals. For the full bounded finite-type class, the proved inverse-modulus result is the bracket \(c\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\leq\Omega_{k,m}(\varepsilon)\leq C\varepsilon^{k/((k+n/2)(m+1))}\); the matching full-class upper exponent remains open in \(\mathrm{oeq:full\text{-}incompressible\text{-}rigidity}\). The radial subclass is sharp at \(\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\). In the primary two-node \(C^2\) Morse case, this means a full-class \(3/4\) lower exponent versus a \(1/3\) upper exponent, with a sharp radial exponent \(3/4\). Zero-law componentwise circular recovery follows from the direct torus identification argument, not from a converse characterization of \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}\). The certified Fourier estimator and representing-model diameter of the quotient-valued confidence set inherit the conservative exponent, giving the primary rate \(N^{-1/12}\).
gap: CauCA and score-based causal representation learning establish componentwise exact identification under almost-everywhere intervention discrepancy, but they do not metrize approximate recovery symmetrically or quantify isolated critical zeros. Quantitative Morse perturbation results requiring higher smoothness do not justify the primary \(C^2\) case, and near-isometry robustness controls a different primitive defect.
fill: The project proves the synthetic product reduction, validates a genuine symmetric quotient geometry, audits the two-node Hamiltonian Morse construction environment by environment, establishes the precise radial restricted frontier, maps its strengthened rate assumptions to the retained exact-identification hypotheses, and targets the nonradial rigidity step needed for estimation and confidence sets.
